TITLE:
Economies of Scale:
Why Bigger Gets Cheaper — Until It Doesn’t
LEAD: Spread a fixed cost over more units and the cost per unit falls — until coordination overhead and bottlenecks push it back up. Biology found the same curve: a mouse burns far more energy per gram than an elephant (metabolic rate scales as mass<sup>¾</sup>), yet no animal grows without limit, because the square–cube law eventually starves the middle.
